deep.reconstruction:
This page works through the smallest test case of the combinatorial ('cartographic') encoding that Grothendieck was applying to pseudoline systems in this dossier.

**Encoding.** A cell decomposition of a surface is coded by a finite set of 'repères' (flags) with involutions σ0, σ1, σ2. Here the configuration is a segment from −1 to +1 cut at its midpoint 0 into two pieces a=[−1,0] and b=[0,+1]. Each piece has two sides (+, −), giving 4 repères a+, a−, b+, b−. The tally reads: (corrected) 2 sommets, 1 face, 2 arêtes, (corrected) 4 repères 'corresponding to the sides of the edges a, b'.

**Barycentric picture.** The left drawing ('subdivision barycentrique') places this on the sphere P^1(C). The real circle carries the points −1, 0, +1, ∞, the upper and lower hemispheres are the sides ±, and a meridian runs 0–∞. The 4 repères are the 4 triangles with vertices {±1, 0, ∞}.

**Involutions.**
- σ0 = σ2 =: σ' swaps a+↔a− and b+↔b− (reflection in the real axis).
- σ1 swaps a+↔b+ and a−↔b− (reflection in the meridian 0∞).
- σ swaps a+↔b− and b+↔a− (rotation by π about 0/∞).

The group generated is the Klein four-group {1, σ', σ, σσ'}. He notes σ' commutes with σ and σ1 = σσ' (the crossed-out σ = σ1σ' is also true). σ2σ0 = 1 here, so the extra involution σ of the previous page's diagram (on the pairs (σ1,σ), (σ2,σ0), …) is realised by the half-turn.

**Relabelling.** The standard generators are rewritten as (σ1, σ, σ2, σ0) = (σσ', σ, σ', σ'). He then defines a 'variante' on the same 4-element set: σ0' = σσ', σ1' = σ', σ2' = σ.
- Check: σ0'σ2' = σσ'σ = σ', an involution, so the axiom (σ0σ2)^2 = 1 holds.
- Every pair of the primed generators generates the whole group, so there is 1 vertex, 1 edge and 1 face, giving χ = 1.
- So the variant is the minimal map on the real projective plane: one closed pseudoline with one vertex.
- This matches the top-right sketch: a hemisphere (RP^2 model) with −1, 0, +1 on the boundary circle.

**Other sketches.** The bottom drawings (sphere with 0 at top, ∞ at bottom, ±1 on the equator, meridians) are the sphere/double-cover pictures of these structures.

**Purpose.** This is calibration of the flag formalism on the degenerate case of one pseudoline, before the wiring-diagram/grid encodings of arrangements on the next page.
errors: Counting: with 2 vertices, 1 face and 2 'arêtes' the Euler characteristic is 1, which is inconsistent with the sphere picture unless 'arêtes' means the half-edges a, b of a single edge [−1,+1]. Four repères (one per side of a, b) is likewise consistent only with 'arête' = half-edge (barycentric triangles), not full edges with 4 flags each. The terminology on the page is loose, not mathematically wrong.

Index convention: σ1 here is the involution exchanging a and b, i.e. the one the standard convention (Esquisse / Malgoire–Voisin) would call σ0. Grothendieck's indices on this page are permuted relative to the usual one; in this abelian example the inconsistency is harmless.

ideas.what: Encoding a map / cell decomposition by a set of flags (triangles of the barycentric subdivision) with three involutions σ0, σ1, σ2 satisfying (σ0σ2)^2 = 1
ideas.modern_name: cartographic group / flag representation of maps (combinatorial maps, Tutte–Lins gem-type encodings)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on dessins and the cartographic group

ideas.what: Worked degenerate example: single edge on the sphere, 4 flags, Klein four-group, with the half-turn σ as the extra involution σ0σ2-type element
ideas.modern_name: trivial/minimal dessin (the map of z ↦ z^2 type, degree-small examples)

ideas.what: Re-labelling the same Klein-four permutation group as a different cartographic structure, yielding the 1-vertex/1-edge/1-face map on RP^2 (a single pseudoline), related to the sphere picture by orientation double cover
ideas.modern_name: non-orientable maps via flag systems; hemi-maps; orientable double cover; Wilson-type operations permuting σ-labels

missed.claim: The page documents Grothendieck applying his flag/cartographic formalism to RP^2 (single pseudoline) as a base case for encoding pseudoline arrangements. Combinatorial treatment of pseudoline arrangements as maps on RP^2 via flag involutions is not usually associated with Grothendieck. The mathematics here is elementary and known in map theory.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical rather than mathematical: it shows the dessins/cartographic machinery was the intended language for the 'pseudo-droites' project.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of a trivial map in the flag formalism already published in the Esquisse; it is interesting only as context for the pseudoline project.
transcription_corrections: '1 face' and '2 arêtes' read correctly; the corrected counts '2 sommets' and '4 repères' are right.
The second line of the top diagram is a crossed-out redrawing of the segment (a+, b+, b−, −1), not content.
The label under the bottom-left sketch is likely 'σ variante' or similar; the sketch is a sphere with 0 at top and 0/∞ at bottom.
In the bottom-right sphere the labels are 0 (top), ∞ (bottom), −1 (left), +1 (right).
